scenes.tts: One protein pulls some growing axons toward the midline of the spinal cord. It pushes others away. What decides?
scenes.visual: Title card: The Map and the Puzzle. Two axons leave the same point; one curves toward a midline marked netrin, the other curves away. Question on screen: what decides?
scenes.narration: One protein pulls some growing axons toward the midline of the spinal cord. It pushes others away. What decides?

scenes.tts: A growing axon is led by its growth cone, the moving, sensing tip at its end.
scenes.visual: A single axon with a fan-shaped growth cone at its tip, fine protrusions reaching out. Label: growth cone.
scenes.narration: A growing axon is led by its growth cone, the moving, sensing tip at its end.

scenes.tts: Now the map. Picture the embryonic spinal cord cut crosswise, like a slice through a tube.
scenes.visual: A tube drawn in perspective; a knife plane cuts across it and the slice rotates to face the viewer. Label: transverse section.
scenes.narration: Now the map. Picture the embryonic spinal cord cut crosswise, like a slice through a tube.

scenes.tts: At the bottom sits the floor plate. It is a strip of cells along the ventral midline.
scenes.visual: The slice outline with a small wedge of cells highlighted at the bottom midline. Label: floor plate, ventral midline.
scenes.narration: At the bottom sits the floor plate. It is a strip of cells along the ventral midline.

scenes.tts: The ventricular zone lines the central canal. Its cells are progenitors, dividing cells that make neurons and glia.
scenes.visual: A ring of cells around the central canal lights up. Label: ventricular zone, progenitors.
scenes.narration: The ventricular zone lines the central canal. Its cells are progenitors, dividing cells that make neurons and glia.

scenes.tts: Each progenitor sends a long fibre outward to the edge of the cord.
scenes.visual: Thin radial fibres extend from the ventricular zone cells to the outer edge of the slice.
scenes.narration: Each progenitor sends a long fibre outward to the edge of the cord.

scenes.tts: That outer edge is the pial surface. A basement membrane covers it, a thin sheet of extracellular matrix.
scenes.visual: The outer rim of the slice is traced in a contrasting colour. Labels: pial surface, basement membrane.
scenes.narration: That outer edge is the pial surface. A basement membrane covers it, a thin sheet of extracellular matrix.

scenes.tts: Many commissural neurons sit in the dorsal cord. Their axons grow ventrally, close to the pial surface.
scenes.visual: A neuron in the dorsal cord sends an axon down along the outer edge toward the ventral side. Label: commissural neuron.
scenes.narration: Many commissural neurons sit in the dorsal cord. Their axons grow ventrally, close to the pial surface.

scenes.tts: Then they turn inward to the floor plate and cross it to the other side.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. The axon turns in and crosses the floor plate to the opposite side.
scenes.narration: Then they turn inward to the floor plate and cross it to the other side.

scenes.tts: Add a second traveller, on its own map. This is the neural tube where midbrain meets hindbrain. There, trochlear motor axons start near the ventral midline and grow dorsally, away from the floor plate.
scenes.visual: An inset opens beside the spinal map: a second cross-section, labelled midbrain-hindbrain junction. A trochlear neuron near its ventral midline sends an axon, in another colour, dorsally away from the floor plate. Labels: trochlear motor axons; a separate region.
scenes.narration: Add a second traveller, on its own map. This is the neural tube where midbrain meets hindbrain. There, trochlear motor axons start near the ventral midline and grow dorsally, away from the floor plate.

scenes.tts: Add a third. In the worm C elegans, cells and pioneer axons migrate between the ventral and dorsal sides.
scenes.caption: Add a third. In the worm C. elegans, cells and pioneer axons migrate between the ventral and dorsal sides.
scenes.visual: A worm in cross-section, ventral side down. Small cells and pioneer axons move up and down between ventral and dorsal. Label: C. elegans.
scenes.narration: Add a third. In the worm C. elegans, cells and pioneer axons migrate between the ventral and dorsal sides.

scenes.tts: The worm's netrin, called U N C six, is made on the ventral side.
scenes.caption: The worm's netrin, called UNC-6, is made on the ventral side.
scenes.visual: A glowing band along the worm's ventral side. Label: UNC-6, made ventrally.
scenes.narration: The worm's netrin, called UNC-6, is made on the ventral side.

scenes.tts: The map raises three puzzles. First, a floor plate in a gel draws axons from dorsal cord without touching it. What crosses?
scenes.visual: Box 1 fills: two explants in a gel, axons curving from one toward the other across a gap. Text: what crosses the gel?
scenes.narration: The map raises three puzzles. First, a floor plate in a gel draws axons from dorsal cord without touching it. What crosses?

scenes.tts: Second, how can one cue pull commissural axons toward the ventral midline, and push trochlear axons away?
scenes.visual: Box 2 fills: the commissural axon on the spinal map and the trochlear axon in its inset, one growing toward the floor plate and one away. Text: one cue, two answers?
scenes.narration: Second, how can one cue pull commissural axons toward the ventral midline, and push trochlear axons away?

scenes.tts: Third, is the cue a gradient from the midline, or laid along the axons' path?
scenes.visual: Box 3 fills: a shaded gradient spreading from the floor plate beside a dotted band laid along the pial surface. Text: gradient or path?
scenes.narration: Third, is the cue a gradient from the midline, or laid along the axons' path?

scenes.tts: Make a guess. Is the direction written into the cue? Or does the cell that reads it decide?
scenes.visual: Two cards: direction in the cue, direction in the reader. A question mark between them.
scenes.narration: Make a guess. Is the direction written into the cue? Or does the cell that reads it decide?

scenes.tts: This lesson argues for the second. Netrin marks a place. The growth cone decides what to do there.
scenes.visual: The card 'direction in the reader' lights. Rule on screen: netrin marks a place; the growth cone decides what to do there.
scenes.narration: This lesson argues for the second. Netrin marks a place. The growth cone decides what to do there.

scenes.tts: Where netrin is supplies the where: its source, its slope, the surface it lies on.
scenes.visual: Rule card, first line: where = source, slope, surface. Icons for each on the map.
scenes.narration: Where netrin is supplies the where: its source, its slope, the surface it lies on.

scenes.tts: The growth cone supplies the sign. Its receptors come first. D C C usually draws it in. U N C five receptors add repulsion, sometimes with D C C.
scenes.caption: The growth cone supplies the sign. Its receptors come first. DCC usually draws it in. UNC5 receptors add repulsion, sometimes with DCC.
scenes.visual: Rule card, second line: sign = receptors. A growth cone with DCC turning toward netrin; one with UNC5 turning away.
scenes.narration: The growth cone supplies the sign. Its receptors come first. DCC usually draws it in. UNC5 receptors add repulsion, sometimes with DCC.

scenes.tts: In some cells, its internal signalling state counts too, such as cyclic A M P or calcium. Laminin, a matrix protein outside the cell, can change that state.
scenes.caption: In some cells, its internal signalling state counts too, such as cAMP or calcium. Laminin, a matrix protein outside the cell, can change that state.
scenes.visual: Rule card, third line: in some cells, internal state: cAMP, calcium. Laminin is drawn outside the growth cone, on the surface beneath it, with an arrow into the cell.
scenes.narration: In some cells, its internal signalling state counts too, such as cAMP or calcium. Laminin, a matrix protein outside the cell, can change that state.

scenes.tts: The rule has limits. Netrin is not always a long-range gradient. And it does more than steer.
scenes.visual: Two limit tags under the rule card: not always a long-range gradient; does more than steer.
scenes.narration: The rule has limits. Netrin is not always a long-range gradient. And it does more than steer.

scenes.tts: Keep this map in view. Each chapter fills one of the three boxes.
scenes.visual: The transverse spinal cord map: dorsal commissural neurons at top, floor plate at the ventral midline, ventricular zone around the central canal, pial surface at the outer edge, commissural path drawn from dorsal cord down near the pia, then in across the floor plate. The trochlear inset sits beside it. Three empty boxes wait under the map.
scenes.narration: Keep this map in view. Each chapter fills one of the three boxes.
